t: A credit card style Linux computer built on an open RISC-V processor design.
steps: Buy the board from Waveshare or a bundle from Ameridroid. Launch prices were 55 to 85 US dollars, but 2026 listings run much higher.
Get a 9 to 12 V USB-C power-delivery supply and a microSD card.
Download a Debian or Ubuntu image made for the VisionFive 2.
Write the image to the microSD card with a free tool such as Raspberry Pi Imager or balenaEtcher.
Update the U-Boot firmware in SPI flash. Debian needs version 2025.01 or newer.
Connect a network cable and boot the board.
Log in and run a short Python script that prints a message.
Try reading a sensor on the 40-pin header next.
meta: Open Board. From $220. A few stores.
